_meta.name: therapy_library
_meta.status: STAGING — not evidence_registry.json; promote in curated batches after faculty triage confirmation
_meta.generator: Cowork session (Moss) — schema per PLAN_Taplinger B4
_meta.verification: identity + retraction verified via Europe PMC 2026-08-20 for all entries except stanley-brown-2012 (pending Crossref). Canonical Scholar_Sidekick pass pending: checkOpenAccess (Unpaywall), checkRetraction (errata/EoC), formatCitation (ama).

entries.citation: Flückiger C, Del Re AC, Wampold BE, Horvath AO. The alliance in adult psychotherapy: a meta-analytic synthesis. Psychotherapy (Chic). 2018;55(4):316-340.
entries.annotation: The canonical number: alliance quality predicts outcome across hundreds of studies. Read before any modality. Fixes WP-26 miscitation.

entries.citation: Tetzlaff M, Bruins J, Castelein S. Associated factors of the quality of therapeutic alliance in people with severe mental illnesses: a systematic review. Clin Psychol Rev. 2025;122:102656.
entries.annotation: Closest to our census: alliance with SMI patients is buildable, and the levers are partly the clinician's.

entries.citation: Huggett C, Gooding P, Haddock G, Quigley J, Pratt D. The relationship between the therapeutic alliance in psychotherapy and suicidal experiences: a systematic review. Clin Psychol Psychother. 2022;29(4):1203-1235.
entries.annotation: Keeping an alliance alive while assessing suicide risk; assessment done TO a patient erodes what safety planning depends on.

entries.citation: Saxler E, Schindler T, Philipsen A, Schulze M, Lux S. Therapeutic alliance in individual adult psychotherapy: a systematic review of conceptualizations and measures. Front Psychol. 2024;15:1293851.
entries.annotation: Open-access primer on what alliance means (bond/goals/tasks) before the outcome literature.

entries.citation: Huggett C, Peters S, Gooding P, Berry N, Pratt D. A systematic review and meta-ethnography of client and therapist perspectives of the therapeutic alliance in the context of psychotherapy and suicidal experiences. Clin Psychol Rev. 2024;113:102469.
entries.annotation: Go-deeper: qualitative meta-ethnography of both perspectives on alliance amid suicidal experiences (proxy-only).

entries.citation: Difronzo MJ, Thackeray L, O'Keeffe S, Calderon A, Midgley N. "Maybe you don't know what answers I want": unresolved alliance ruptures preceding dropout in short-term psychoanalytic psychotherapy with depressed adolescents. Res Psychother. 2025;28(1):841.
entries.annotation: The only rupture-repair paper in the harvest: unresolved ruptures precede dropout. Cross-filed from evidence-limits.

entries.citation: Man H, Wood L, Glover N. A systematic review and narrative synthesis of indirect psychological intervention in acute mental health inpatient settings. Clin Psychol Psychother. 2023;30(1):24-37.
entries.annotation: Indirect = psychology delivered through the team and milieu — what an acute unit can actually staff.

entries.citation: Schefft C, Guhn A, Brakemeier EL, Sterzer P, Köhler S. Efficacy of inpatient psychotherapy for major depressive disorder: a meta-analysis of controlled trials. Acta Psychiatr Scand. 2019;139(4):322-335.
entries.annotation: Psychotherapy works within an admission for MDD (SMD 0.24, NNT ~7) with zero heterogeneity across modalities.

entries.citation: Cohen-Chazani Y, Lavidor M, Gilboa-Schechtman E, Roe D, Hasson-Ohayon I. Meta-analysis of the effect of psychotherapy in an inpatient setting. Psychiatry. 2022;85(4):399-417.
entries.annotation: Across diagnoses: real effect (d≈0.43), moderated by diagnosis more than by therapy brand — common factors carry it.

entries.citation: Cuijpers P, Ciharova M, Tong L, et al. Behavioral activation for depression: a comprehensive systematic review and meta-analysis. Clin Psychol Rev. 2026;128:102783.
entries.annotation: Current state of the whole BA field — same first author as the 2007 anchor, twenty years on.

entries.citation: Cuijpers P, van Straten A, Warmerdam L. Behavioral activation treatments of depression: a meta-analysis. Clin Psychol Rev. 2007;27(3):318-326.
entries.annotation: Where the modern claim started: activation alone is a treatment, not a warm-up for cognitive work.

entries.citation: Ciharova M, Furukawa TA, Efthimiou O, et al. Cognitive restructuring, behavioral activation and cognitive-behavioral therapy in the treatment of adult depression: a network meta-analysis. J Consult Clin Psychol. 2021;89(6):563-574.
entries.annotation: The dismantling question head-to-head: how much does the C in CBT add over activation alone?

entries.citation: Simmonds-Buckley M, Kellett S, Waller G. Acceptability and efficacy of group behavioral activation for depression among adults: a meta-analysis. Behav Ther. 2019;50(5):864-885.
entries.annotation: The evidence under the delivery format the unit actually runs: the group.

entries.citation: Pott SL, Delgadillo J, Kellett S. Is behavioral activation an effective and acceptable treatment for co-occurring depression and substance use disorders? A meta-analysis of RCTs. J Subst Abuse Treat. 2022;132:108478.
entries.annotation: Dual diagnosis is the daily census: activation works when depression is entangled with substance use.

entries.citation: Stanley B, Brown GK, Brenner LA, et al. Comparison of the Safety Planning Intervention with follow-up vs usual care of suicidal patients treated in the emergency department. JAMA Psychiatry. 2018;75(9):894-900.
entries.annotation: The foundational SPI cohort: ~45% fewer suicidal behaviors, doubled engagement. The tool's origin citation.

entries.citation: Stanley B, Brown GK. Safety planning intervention: a brief intervention to mitigate suicide risk. Cogn Behav Pract. 2012;19(2):256-264.
entries.annotation: The original SPI description. Not Europe PMC-indexed (Cogn Behav Pract) — verify via Crossref/verifyCitation.
entries.note: verification: PENDING (not in Europe PMC; run verifyCitation via Scholar_Sidekick)

entries.citation: Steeg S, Ledden S, Marzano L, et al. Effectiveness of suicide means restriction: an overview of systematic reviews. BMJ Ment Health. 2025;28(1):e302069.
entries.annotation: Umbrella view: restricting access to lethal means changes outcomes, not just process measures.

entries.citation: Shank LM, Smolenski DJ, Boyd C, et al. Systematic review of the impact of interventions changing access to lethal means on suicide attempts and deaths. Inj Prev. 2026;32(1):7-15.
entries.annotation: The depth behind the umbrella — the citation under every secure-the-home conversation.

entries.citation: Penzenik ME, Schneider AL, Hoffmire CA, Sells JR, Stearns-Yoder KA, Brenner LA. Rural community members' experiences and perceptions regarding lethal means safety. J Rural Health. 2026;42(1):e70103.
entries.annotation: How rural communities — ours — actually hear lethal-means counseling; the how is population-specific.

entries.citation: Varese F, Sudell M, Morrison AP, Longden E, Tudur Smith C; IMPART. Treatment effect modifiers of cognitive behaviour therapy in people with psychosis: an IPD meta-analysis of RCTs. Health Technol Assess. 2025;29(53):1-115.
entries.annotation: IPD answer to who benefits from CBTp: average effects hide heterogeneity; selection is a skill.

entries.citation: Hong Y, Chen Y, Bai Y, Tan W. Cognitive-behavioral therapy for the improvement of negative symptoms and functioning in schizophrenia: SR and meta-analysis of RCTs. PLoS One. 2025;20(5):e0324685.
entries.annotation: The honest quantification of the hardest target: negative symptoms.

entries.citation: Tarrier N, Wykes T. Is there evidence that cognitive behaviour therapy is an effective treatment for schizophrenia? A cautious or cautionary tale? Behav Res Ther. 2004;42(12):1377-1401.
entries.annotation: Effect sizes shrink as rigor rises — the most transferable methods lesson in the library.

entries.citation: Links PS, Ross J. Good psychiatric management of borderline personality disorder: foundations and future challenges. Am J Psychother. 2025;78(1):4-10.
entries.annotation: The reframe that changes behavior: BPD is treatable by any competent generalist. Refer-out is not a plan.

entries.citation: Wibbelink CJM, Kamphuis JH, Sinnaeve R, et al. Dialectical behavior therapy vs schema therapy for patients with borderline personality disorder: the BOOTS multicenter randomized clinical trial. JAMA Psychiatry. 2026;83(7):669-681.
entries.annotation: The newest head-to-head of two specialist therapies (equivalence trial design).

entries.citation: Brodsky BS, Galfalvy H, Mann JJ, Grunebaum MF, Stanley B. Dialectical behavior therapy versus serotonin reuptake inhibitor treatment for suicidal behavior in borderline personality disorder: an RCT. Am J Psychiatry. 2025;182(12):1083-1092.
entries.annotation: Meds-versus-therapy tested where it matters most: suicidal behavior in BPD.

entries.citation: Arqueros M, Soler J, Pascual JC. Stand-alone dialectical behavior therapy skills training for borderline personality disorder: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Personal Disord. 2026 (ahead of print).
entries.annotation: What the affordable, skills-only version buys — a discharge-planning fact.

entries.citation: Appel G, Arac-Orhun S, Hersh R. Guidance for family engagement with patients with borderline personality disorder. Psychodyn Psychiatry. 2026;54(1):97-109.
entries.annotation: The family is usually in the room and rarely addressed; TFP+GPM principles for engaging them.

entries.citation: Pharoah F, Mari J, Rathbone J, Wong W. Family intervention for schizophrenia. Cochrane Database Syst Rev. 2010;(12):CD000088.
entries.annotation: The canonical Cochrane: less relapse, fewer readmissions, better adherence. NNT ~7 territory.

entries.citation: Ma CF, Chan SKW, Chung YL, et al. The predictive power of expressed emotion and its components in relapse of schizophrenia: meta-analysis and meta-regression. Psychol Med. 2021;51(3):365-375.
entries.annotation: The family's emotional climate is a measured, modifiable relapse predictor — the floor under all family work.

entries.citation: Camacho-Gomez M, Castellvi P. Effectiveness of family intervention for preventing relapse in first-episode psychosis until 24 months of follow-up. Schizophr Bull. 2020;46(1):98-109.
entries.annotation: Intervene early with families in FEP and relapse falls, durably to 24 months.

entries.citation: Schwenker R, Dietrich CE, Hirpa S, et al. Motivational interviewing for substance use reduction. Cochrane Database Syst Rev. 2023;12:CD008063.
entries.annotation: The definitive review, valuable for its restraint: modest effects, limited certainty. Stance plus calibration.

entries.citation: Bastos Maia M, Martins PM, Figueiredo-Braga M. Outcomes and challenges of motivational interviewing in dual diagnosis treatment: a systematic review. J Dual Diagn. 2025;21(1):56-69.
entries.annotation: The MI paper that matches our census: dual diagnosis.

entries.citation: Ferguson M, Loughhead M, McIntyre H, Procter N. Trauma-informed approaches to suicide prevention. Crisis. 2026;47(1):41-52.
entries.annotation: The bridge between trauma histories and risk practices: assessment can retraumatize; there are alternatives.

entries.citation: Goldstein E, Chokshi B, Melendez-Torres GJ, Rios A, Jelley M, Lewis-O'Connor A. Effectiveness of trauma-informed care implementation in health care settings: systematic review of reviews and realist synthesis. Perm J. 2024;28(1):135-150.
entries.annotation: What actually happens when systems implement TIC — the freely linkable workhorse.

entries.citation: Mahon D. An umbrella review of systematic reviews on trauma informed approaches. Community Ment Health J. 2024;60(8):1627-1651.
entries.annotation: The honest status report at the highest evidence tier: enthusiasm currently outruns outcome evidence.

entries.citation: Hajek Gross C, Oehlke SM, Prillinger K, Goreis A, Plener PL, Kothgassner OD. Efficacy of mentalization-based therapy in treating self-harm: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Suicide Life Threat Behav. 2024;54(2):317-337.
entries.annotation: A psychodynamically derived treatment with meta-analytic support for self-harm.

entries.citation: Wienicke FJ, Beutel ME, Zwerenz R, et al. Efficacy and moderators of short-term psychodynamic psychotherapy for depression: SR and meta-analysis of individual participant data. Clin Psychol Rev. 2023;101:102269.
entries.annotation: Retires the reflex that psychodynamic means unevidenced — IPD-level support in depression.

entries.citation: Driessen E, Fokkema M, Dekker JJM, et al. Which patients benefit from adding short-term psychodynamic psychotherapy to antidepressants in the treatment of depression? Psychol Med. 2023;53(13):6090-6101.
entries.annotation: The combined-treatment question in its most ward-relevant form: who gains from adding therapy to the antidepressant?

entries.citation: de Figueiredo JM. The demoralization construct in clinical practice and research. J Clin Psychiatry. 2026;87(2):26com16383.
entries.annotation: The highest-yield CL distinction: demoralization is not depression. (Commentary; author spelling per EPMC 'de Figueirido' — resolve at formatCitation.)

entries.citation: Gunturu S, McGee M, Javaid A. Meaning-Centered Psychotherapy. In: StatPearls. StatPearls Publishing; 2026. NBK622746.
entries.annotation: Free reference orientation to meaning-centered psychotherapy before the trial literature.

entries.citation: Abbass A, Town J, Holmes H, et al. Short-term psychodynamic psychotherapy for functional somatic disorders: a meta-analysis of RCTs. Psychother Psychosom. 2020;89(6):363-370.
entries.annotation: Functional somatic presentations are consult bread-and-butter; a specific therapy helps.

entries.citation: Modini M, Large M. Understanding the suicide rate post-discharge from a psychiatric hospital: time for a rethink. Australas Psychiatry. 2026;34(3):227-230.
entries.annotation: The statistic to carry out of the rotation: risk peaks in the weeks after discharge.

entries.citation: Diefenbach GJ, Collett S, Black S, Rudd MD, Gueorguieva R, Tolin DF. The effect of inpatient brief CBT for suicide prevention on post-discharge emergency department utilization. Gen Hosp Psychiatry. 2025;93:73-79.
entries.annotation: What is delivered during the stay bends the curve after it (secondary analysis of the BCBT-Inpatient RCT).

entries.citation: Steinberg R, Amini J, Sinyor M, Mitchell RHB, Schaffer A. Implementation of caring contacts using patient feedback to reduce suicide-related outcomes following psychiatric hospitalization. Suicide Life Threat Behav. 2024;54(6):1041-1052.
entries.annotation: One of the cheapest interventions in psychiatry, refined with patient input.

entries.citation: Schünemann O, Jansen A, Willutzki U, Heinrichs N. Allegiance and treatment quality as moderators of the comparative effectiveness of psychotherapy? Clin Psychol Eur. 2025;7(1):e9709.
entries.annotation: Who ran the trial shapes what it finds (scope: humanistic-vs-other comparisons). Read author lists like methods.

entries.citation: De Salve F, Rossi C, Gioacchini E, Messina I, Oasi O. Dropout in psychotherapy for personality disorders: a systematic review of predictors. Clin Psychol Psychother. 2025;32(3):e70080.
entries.annotation: The outcome nobody advertises: a therapy the patient leaves is not a therapy that worked.

entries.citation: Westra HA. The implications of the Dodo bird verdict for training in psychotherapy: prioritizing process observation. Psychother Res. 2023;33(4):527-529.
entries.annotation: If therapies are near-equivalent on average, what should you train? The closing read of the section.

entries.citation: Xia J, Merinder LB, Belgamwar MR. Psychoeducation for schizophrenia. Cochrane Database Syst Rev. 2011;(6):CD002831.
entries.annotation: Psychoeducation in schizophrenia: NNT ~5 readmission, ~9 relapse — strongest single inpatient psychological intervention.

entries.citation: Kleiman EM, Hawes-Sousa MT, Rizvi SL, Nock MK. Updating psychological treatment during inpatient psychiatric care. JAMA Psychiatry. 2026;83(6):559-560.
entries.annotation: The redesign argument: stand-alone transdiagnostic modules targeting four crisis mechanisms.

entries.citation: Diefenbach GJ, Lord KA, Stubbing J, et al. Brief cognitive behavioral therapy for suicidal inpatients: a randomized clinical trial. JAMA Psychiatry. 2024;81(12):1177-1186.
entries.annotation: The primary BCBT-Inpatient RCT behind the post-discharge secondary analysis; spine candidate.

entries.citation: Kearns JC, Crasta D, Spitzer EG, et al. Evaluating the effectiveness of safety plans for mitigating suicide risk in two samples of psychiatrically hospitalized military veterans. Behav Ther. 2025;56(2):438-451.
entries.annotation: Safety-plan quality (especially warning signs) predicts outcomes; completion alone is false reassurance.

entries.citation: Sall J, Brenner L, Millikan Bell AM, Colston MJ. Assessment and management of patients at risk for suicide: synopsis of the 2019 VA/DoD clinical practice guidelines. Ann Intern Med. 2019;171(5):343-353.
entries.annotation: VA/DoD guideline synopsis: SPI standard of care; no-suicide contracts out.

entries.citation: Belkin MR, Briggs MC, Candan K, et al. Psychoeducation for inpatients with first-episode psychosis: results from a survey of psychiatry trainees. Psychiatr Serv. 2021;72(5):582-585.
entries.annotation: The practice gap: most 'psychoeducation' is unstructured conversation — structure and document it.

entries.citation: Linehan MM, Korslund KE, Harned MS, et al. Dialectical behavior therapy for high suicide risk in individuals with borderline personality disorder: an RCT and component analysis. JAMA Psychiatry. 2015;72(5):475-482.
entries.annotation: The dismantling RCT: skills training is the active ingredient — legitimizes skills-only groups on the unit.

entries.citation: Bohus M, Stoffers-Winterling J, Sharp C, Krause-Utz A, Schmahl C, Lieb K. Borderline personality disorder. Lancet. 2021;398(10310):1528-1540.
entries.annotation: The Lancet seminar: crisis intervention outpatient when possible; distress-tolerance first for high distress.

entries.citation: Leichsenring F, Heim N, Leweke F, Spitzer C, Steinert C, Kernberg OF. Borderline personality disorder: a review. JAMA. 2023;329(8):670-679.
entries.annotation: The JAMA review: consistent team approach for splitting; BPD affective storms are not comorbid mood disorders.

entries.citation: Soler J, Casellas-Pujol E, Fernández-Felipe I, et al. "Skills for pills": the dialectical-behavioural therapy skills training reduces polypharmacy in borderline personality disorder. Acta Psychiatr Scand. 2022;145(4):332-342.
entries.annotation: Skills for pills: teaching coping skills reduces polypharmacy — deprescription as a therapeutic intervention.

entries.citation: Tham SS, Solomon P. Family involvement in routine services for individuals with severe mental illness: scoping review of barriers and strategies. Psychiatr Serv. 2024;75(10):1009-1030.
entries.annotation: The implementation paradox quantified: the main barrier to family involvement is clinician avoidance.

entries.citation: Hansson KM, Romøren M, Weimand B, et al. The duty of confidentiality during family involvement: ethical challenges and possible solutions. BMC Psychiatry. 2022;22(1):812.
entries.annotation: Listening is not disclosing: the confidentiality reframe that unlocks family involvement.
